description.it: Creare un Secret per credenziali database
description.en: Create a Secret for database credentials

exercises.task:
1. Crea un Secret 'db-secret' nel namespace default
2. Includi: username=admin, password=secret123
3. Verifica che sia creato correttamente
4. Decodifica i valori per verificarne il contenuto
exercises.solution:
kubectl create secret generic db-secret --from-literal=username=admin --from-literal=password=secret123
kubectl get secret db-secret
kubectl get secret db-secret -o jsonpath='{.data.username}' | base64 -d && echo
kubectl get secret db-secret -o jsonpath='{.data.password}' | base64 -d && echo
exercises.validation: kubectl get secret db-secret -o jsonpath='{.data.username}' | base64 -d

description.it: Iniettare credenziali da Secret in un Pod
description.en: Inject credentials from Secret into a Pod

exercises.task:
1. Crea un Pod 'secret-pod' con immagine busybox
2. Usa le credenziali dal Secret 'db-secret' come env vars
3. Esegui: env | grep DB_
4. Verifica che i valori siano presenti
hints: Specificare name del Secret e key
exercises.solution:
kubectl apply -f - << 'EOF'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: secret-pod
spec:
  containers:
  - name: test
    image: busybox
    command: ['sh', '-c', 'env | grep DB && sleep 3600']
    env:
    - name: DB_USERNAME
      valueFrom:
        secretKeyRef:
          name: db-secret
          key: username
    - name: DB_PASSWORD
      valueFrom:
        secretKeyRef:
          name: db-secret
          key: password
EOF

kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready pod/secret-pod --timeout=30s
kubectl exec secret-pod -- env | grep DB

description.it: Generare certificato auto-firmato e creare Secret TLS
description.en: Generate self-signed certificate and create TLS Secret

exercises.task:
1. Genera un certificato TLS auto-firmato (openssl)
2. Crea un Secret 'tls-secret' di tipo kubernetes.io/tls
3. Verifica che i campi tls.crt e tls.key siano presenti
4. Controlla il tipo del Secret
hints: kubectl get secret -o yaml mostra il tipo
exercises.solution:
# Genera certificato
openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -keyout key.pem -out cert.pem \
  -days 365 -nodes -subj '/CN=localhost'

# Crea Secret
kubectl create secret tls tls-secret --cert=cert.pem --key=key.pem

# Verifica
kubectl get secret tls-secret -o jsonpath='{.type}'
kubectl get secret tls-secret -o jsonpath='{.data.tls\.crt}' | base64 -d | openssl x509 -text -noout | head

description.it: Accedere al Secret come file nel container
description.en: Access Secret as files in the container

exercises.task:
1. Crea un Pod con volume montato da 'db-secret'
2. Monta in /etc/secrets
3. Verifica che i file siano presenti e leggibili
4. Controlla i permessi dei file
exercises.solution:
kubectl apply -f - << 'EOF'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: secret-volume-pod
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox
    command: ['sh', '-c', 'while true; do ls -la /etc/secrets; sleep 60; done']
    volumeMounts:
    - name: secrets
      mountPath: /etc/secrets
      readOnly: true
  volumes:
  - name: secrets
    secret:
      name: db-secret
      defaultMode: 0400
EOF

kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready pod/secret-volume-pod --timeout=30s
kubectl exec secret-volume-pod -- ls -la /etc/secrets

description.it: Impostare contesto di sicurezza per un Pod
description.en: Set security context for a Pod

exercises.task:
1. Crea un Pod 'secure-pod' con immagine nginx
2. Imposta runAsUser: 1000, runAsGroup: 3000
3. Imposta runAsNonRoot: true
4. Imposta readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
5. Verifica che il container non giri come root
hints: securityContext a livello Pod e container
runAsNonRoot fallisce se l'immagine richiede root
nginx:alpine funziona come non-root con config
exercises.solution:
kubectl apply -f - << 'EOF'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: secure-pod
spec:
  securityContext:
    runAsUser: 1000
    runAsGroup: 3000
    runAsNonRoot: true
    fsGroup: 2000
  containers:
  - name: nginx
    image: nginx:alpine
    securityContext:
      readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
      allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
      capabilities:
        drop: ['ALL']
    volumeMounts:
    - name: cache
      mountPath: /var/cache/nginx
    - name: run
      mountPath: /var/run
  volumes:
  - name: cache
    emptyDir: {}
  - name: run
    emptyDir: {}
EOF

kubectl exec secure-pod -- id

description.it: Configurare un ServiceAccount dedicato per un Pod
description.en: Configure a dedicated ServiceAccount for a Pod

exercises.task:
1. Crea un ServiceAccount 'app-sa'
2. Crea un Pod che usa questo ServiceAccount
3. Verifica che il token sia montato
4. Controlla i mount nel container
exercises.solution:
kubectl create serviceaccount app-sa

kubectl apply -f - << 'EOF'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: sa-pod
spec:
  serviceAccountName: app-sa
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox
    command: ['sh', '-c', 'ls -la /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/ && sleep 3600']
EOF

kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready pod/sa-pod --timeout=30s
kubectl exec sa-pod -- ls /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/

description.it: Configurare permessi RBAC per un ServiceAccount
description.en: Configure RBAC permissions for a ServiceAccount

exercises.task:
1. Crea una Role 'pod-reader' per leggere Pod
2. Crea un RoleBinding che collega app-sa a pod-reader
3. Testa l'accesso con kubectl auth can-i
4. Verifica che possa leggere ma non creare Pod
exercises.solution:
kubectl apply -f - << 'EOF'
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: pod-reader
rules:
- apiGroups: ['']
  resources: ['pods']
  verbs: ['get', 'list', 'watch']
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: app-sa-pod-reader
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: app-sa
roleRef:
  kind: Role
  name: pod-reader
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
EOF

kubectl auth can-i list pods --as=system:serviceaccount:default:app-sa
kubectl auth can-i create pods --as=system:serviceaccount:default:app-sa

description.it: Bloccare tutto il traffico in ingresso/uscita

exercises.task:
1. Crea un namespace 'secured'
2. Implementa una NetworkPolicy deny-all
3. Crea un Pod nginx e testa l'accesso
4. Verifica che il traffico è bloccato
exercises.solution:
kubectl create namespace secured

kubectl apply -n secured -f - << 'EOF'
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-all
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Ingress
  - Egress
EOF

kubectl run -n secured nginx --image=nginx:alpine
kubectl wait -n secured --for=condition=Ready pod/nginx --timeout=30s

# Test connessione (dovrebbe fallire con network policy)
kubectl run -n secured test --image=busybox --rm -it --restart=Never -- wget -qO- http://nginx
exercises.validation: kubectl get networkpolicy -n secured deny-all -o jsonpath='{.spec.policyTypes}'

description.it: Configurare regole allow per traffico selezionato
description.en: Configure allow rules for selected traffic

exercises.task:
1. Crea una NetworkPolicy che permette traffico da Pod con label 'app=frontend'
2. Permetti traffico solo sulla porta 80
3. Testa da un Pod frontend e uno non autorizzato
4. Verifica che solo frontend può connettersi
hints: I selector sono AND tra loro
exercises.solution:
kubectl apply -n secured -f - << 'EOF'
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-frontend
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nginx
  policyTypes:
  - Ingress
  ingress:
  - from:
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: frontend
    ports:
    - port: 80
EOF

kubectl run -n secured frontend --image=busybox --labels=app=frontend -- sh -c 'wget -qO- http://nginx && sleep 3600'
kubectl run -n secured backend --image=busybox --labels=app=backend -- sh -c 'wget -qO- http://nginx || echo Failed'
exercises.validation: kubectl get networkpolicy -n secured allow-frontend -o yaml | grep -A 5 'ingress:'

exercises.task:
1. Crea un Secret 'regcred' per un registry privato (simulato)
2. Configura il Secret come imagePullSecrets in un Pod
3. Verifica la configurazione
4. Controlla il tipo del Secret
exercises.solution:
kubectl create secret docker-registry regcred \
  --docker-server=registry.example.com \
  --docker-username=admin \
  --docker-password=password123 \
  --docker-email=admin@example.com

kubectl apply -f - << 'EOF'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: private-pod
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: registry.example.com/myapp:v1
  imagePullSecrets:
  - name: regcred
EOF

kubectl get secret regcred -o jsonpath='{.type}'

description.it: Forzare PSS Restricted su un namespace
description.en: Enforce PSS Restricted on a namespace

exercises.task:
1. Crea un namespace 'restricted'
2. Applica l'annotazione PSS restricted
3. Prova a creare un Pod senza security context
4. Verifica che venga rifiutato
hints: I Pod esistenti non vengono eliminati
exercises.solution:
kubectl create namespace restricted
kubectl label namespace restricted pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce=restricted

# Questo fallirà o genererà warning
kubectl apply -n restricted -f - << 'EOF'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: insecure-pod
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: nginx
EOF

kubectl get namespace restricted -o jsonpath='{.metadata.labels}'

exercises.task:
1. Crea un Pod con capabilities drop ALL
2. Aggiungi solo CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE
3. Verifica che non può fare operazioni privilegiate
4. Testa binding su porta 80 (richiede capability)
hints: La maggior parte delle app non necessita capabilities
exercises.solution:
kubectl apply -f - << 'EOF'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: caps-pod
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: nginx:alpine
    securityContext:
      capabilities:
        drop: ['ALL']
        add: ['NET_BIND_SERVICE']
    ports:
    - containerPort: 80
EOF

kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready pod/caps-pod --timeout=30s
kubectl exec caps-pod -- capsh --print

exercises.task:
1. Crea un ServiceAccount 'no-mount-sa' con automount disabilitato
2. Crea un Pod che usa questo SA
3. Verifica che la directory del token non esiste
4. Confronta con un Pod che ha automount abilitato
hints: Il Pod può sovrascrivere il default del SA
Sicurezza: usare solo se il Pod non parla con API
exercises.solution:
kubectl apply -f - << 'EOF'
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: no-mount-sa
automountServiceAccountToken: false
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: no-mount-pod
spec:
  serviceAccountName: no-mount-sa
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox
    command: ['sh', '-c', 'ls -la /var/run/secrets/ 2>&1 || echo "No secrets"; sleep 3600']
EOF

kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready pod/no-mount-pod --timeout=30s
kubectl exec no-mount-pod -- ls /var/run/secrets/ 2>&1 || echo 'No automount'

description.it: Dare accesso read-only a tutto il cluster
description.en: Grant read-only access to entire cluster

exercises.task:
1. Crea un ClusterRole 'cluster-viewer'
2. Crea un ClusterRoleBinding per app-sa
3. Testa che può leggere Pod in tutti i namespace
4. Verifica che non può creare risorse
exercises.solution:
kubectl apply -f - << 'EOF'
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: ClusterRole
metadata:
  name: cluster-viewer
rules:
- apiGroups: ['']
  resources: ['*']
  verbs: ['get', 'list', 'watch']
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: ClusterRoleBinding
metadata:
  name: app-sa-viewer
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: app-sa
  namespace: default
roleRef:
  kind: ClusterRole
  name: cluster-viewer
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
EOF

kubectl auth can-i list pods --all-namespaces --as=system:serviceaccount:default:app-sa

description.it: Applicare tutte le best practice di sicurezza

exercises.task:
1. Crea un Pod con: utente non-root, capabilities minime, filesystem read-only, no privilege escalation
2. Configura NetworkPolicy per isolamento
3. Usa Secret per password
4. Imposta ResourceQuota per limiti
exercises.solution:
kubectl apply -f - << 'EOF'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: app-secret
type: Opaque
stringData:
  password: supersecret
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: secure-app
  labels:
    app: secure
spec:
  securityContext:
    runAsNonRoot: true
    runAsUser: 1000
    fsGroup: 1000
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: nginx:alpine
    securityContext:
      readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
      allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
      capabilities:
        drop: ['ALL']
        add: ['NET_BIND_SERVICE']
    env:
    - name: PASSWORD
      valueFrom:
        secretKeyRef:
          name: app-secret
          key: password
    volumeMounts:
    - name: cache
      mountPath: /var/cache/nginx
    - name: run
      mountPath: /var/run
    resources:
      limits:
        cpu: 500m
        memory: 256Mi
      requests:
        cpu: 100m
        memory: 128Mi
  volumes:
  - name: cache
    emptyDir: {}
  - name: run
    emptyDir: {}
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: secure-isolation
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: secure
  policyTypes: [Ingress, Egress]
  ingress:
  - ports: [{port: 80}]
  egress:
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector: {}
EOF
exercises.validation: kubectl exec secure-app -- id && kubectl exec secure-app -- sh -c 'echo $PASSWORD'
